transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Ava Rodriguez (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Harbor Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (Platform Eng), Sonia Gupta (SecOps), Evan Moore (PM)
---
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you say hi?
00:04 Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here. Sorry for being late, had a back-to-back.
00:06 Tom Alvarez: Tom — platform. All good here.
00:08 Sonia Gupta: Sonia, SecOps.
00:10 Evan Moore: Evan, PM.
00:12 Lena Park: Great. Agenda — usage/costs, recent latency incidents, pilot expansion ask, security artifacts. Marcus will run through the benchmark ask. Ava will cover operational health and billing trends.
00:25 Ava Rodriguez: I'll start with the usage slide — we saw a 38% month-over-month increase in inference calls, but token-per-call also up ~12% because the new summarization flow is longer. Most of the growth is evening PST hours, 18:00-22:00.
00:40 Priya Nair: That matches what we see. We shipped the new agent in late March and traffic shifted. Can you break down by model?
00:48 Ava Rodriguez: Sure — 62% is using gpt-3-esque open model (redwood-default-2), 28% on a quantized variant we recommended, and 10% fallback to hosted high-capacity model during throttles. Note: the model names in reporting sometimes show as redw-infer-v2 in the export, sorry for the mismatch.
01:10 Marcus Chen: About the cost — the main driver is burst fallback. When your dedicated pool hit queue-limits we routed some percent to higher-cost hosted variant. That shows as cost spikes on invoice days. The autoscale policy is set to be conservative, we can tweak to allow controlled bursts or pre-warm.
01:35 Tom Alvarez: We saw a couple of 503s during the April 9 peak — application-level retries made it worse because of retry storms. Can we get better circuit-breaking?
01:45 Marcus Chen: Yep, we have a couple of levers. On Redwood side we can enable per-route rate limits and short-circuit fallbacks to the quantized model instead of hosted fallback. Also prefix KV caching will reduce tokens for repeated prompt patterns.
02:05 Priya Nair: For the user experience we need an upper-bound p95 latency target — anything above 450ms p95 is noticeable. Can you look at that?
02:14 Marcus Chen: We'll run the 48-hour dedicated benchmark with your canonical prompt sets and report p50/p95/p99 and tail latency histograms. Also include cold-start and KV cache warm run.
02:25 Evan Moore: Timeline — if benchmark looks good, we want to expand pilot to 200k monthly queries by mid-June. Cost-neutral ideally.
02:32 Lena Park: Understood. On pricing we can offer a pilot tier with a blended rate while we quantify savings from batching and cache. I'll send a pricing sheet.
02:40 Sonia Gupta: Security — we need encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, SSO/SAML integration, and audit logs stream to our SIEM. Also confirm data deletion SLA for transcripts and cache eviction policy.
02:55 Marcus Chen: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; for hosted we'll provide encrypted storage and an option to rotate keys. Deletion SLA is 30 days for intermediate cache by default; we can discuss shorter retention with a Private deployment. Note: sometimes our product name shows up as RedWood (capital W) in older docs — ignore that, it's the same.
03:20 Priya Nair: Do you have SOC2 and ISO docs we can share with our compliance team?
03:25 Lena Park: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II export and the security whitepaper. Adding Sonia and your compliance contact to the share.
03:32 Tom Alvarez: Back to reliability — what happens if region A gets throttled? We want automatic region failover and no double-billing.
03:40 Marcus Chen: We route by policy — we can configure region-aware routing with failover to a cheaper variant in region B. Billing is aggregated; we'll show a sample chart of routed percent vs cost in the benchmark report.
03:58 Evan Moore: Competitor checks — leadership asked if switching to OpenAI could be cheaper. We checked and the cost is similar at scale, but they lack the Dedicated/Private options. Also Anthropic's newer models have variable latency.
04:18 Lena Park: Right — the differentiation is deterministic latency and the rollout controls for private deployments. We'll show a cost vs latency trade-off curve in the benchmark.
04:30 Priya Nair: A nit — the console trace UI sometimes mislabels routes as 'default-rte', making debugging harder. Any product plans?
04:36 Marcus Chen: We're rolling out a route-id48 mapping in the console next quarter to make traces align to customer-defined route names; timeline is mid-July.
04:48 Ava Rodriguez: On billing detail, we found two invoice anomalies where burst fallback didn't show as 'fallback' label — that made attribution hard. We corrected the YTD view and will send a corrected CSV.
05:04 Sonia Gupta: For the security deep dive, we'll want KMS key policy language and proof of HSM if possible. Also, can you provide redwood's pen-test report?
05:14 Lena Park: We'll include the pen-test summary and redwood's third-party attestation. Marcus will follow up.
05:20 Marcus Chen: Quick technical note: your most common prompt pattern includes a lot of system context — moving static context to the KV cache can shave 20-40% of token usage. We'll highlight recommended batching and cache rules in the benchmark doc.
05:45 Priya Nair: If we reduce token count per call, that might let us hit the 200k target without doubling costs.
05:50 Evan Moore: Ok, next steps as spelled out. Can we reconvene after the benchmark, say May 24?
05:55 Lena Park: Yes, penciled in May 24 15:00 UTC. Thanks everyone.
---
Post-meeting notes (auto): Mentioned artifacts to share: pricing spreadsheet (Lena), benchmark CSV (Marcus), corrected billing CSV (Ava), SOC2 + pen-test summary (Lena), route mapping ETA (Marcus).
